      "observations": [
        "All eight owned paths and every changed hunk were read. The folder override resets mLockedFlags only when the ewsId property is assigned, then maps inbox, deleteditems, drafts, outbox, sentitems, junkemail and archive to the corresponding special-use flag. It delegates property storage to the base method; it does not itself set mFlags. The inspected creation caller assigns the ID before SetFlags.",
        "The landing also exports the incoming server's existing path-based trash getter and changes the folder helper to delegate to it, replacing recursive first-flag lookup. The original helper and accepted helper are separately captured. An empty stored path can yield success with a null result, not a guarantee that a folder exists.",
        "The accepted trash-path setter tries to clear the old folder's Trash flag through ClearFlag, writes the new path, then adds Trash to the new folder. A locked old server folder can retain its flag while another configured folder also has Trash. Actual soft deletion selects the stored path through GetTrashFolder; ancestor Trash flags remain a distinct permanent-delete condition. This is bounded source behavior, not a claim that every multiple-icon or deletion report is cured.",
        "The new sequential mock EWS and Graph tasks check the same six locked flags as IMAP, plus ordinary mutable bits. The outbox/Queue mapping and compound masks are not directly tested. All nine helper assertion call sites have nonempty expected-result messages; missing should alone is not a defect. The two added trash-path assertions have nonempty should messages. Existing subsequent destination-count assertions cover the selected new folder, not removal of the old server folder's locked flag.",
        "The exact accepted shared flag methods and Exchange test-server factories are retained whole from the already-inspected 5627/5631 packets, with original timestamps and source-reader attribution. Their completed common analysis is not counted again. Real-server ID normalization, network protocol equivalence and all provider behavior are not established by these mock cases.",
        "The sparse review corrects an initial assumption that IMAP already enforced these locks: the author points to the preceding IMAP patch. The author later reports a broken test, asks for re-review and receives another acceptance. Those historical phases are separate from this static test/source inspection.",

Later reports about multiple protected folders and last-selected behavior remain explicit. Neither mock tests nor review acceptance prove that every report is resolved.",

Its timeline first corrects the assumption that IMAP already enforces special-use locks, then records an author-reported broken test and a later re-review acceptance. The source specifically adopts distinguished-ID locking and path-based trash selection; those facts are independent of the historical test report."
